meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or corporate law distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed with Islamic Sharia principles; unitary national law; no separate common law system at sub-state level)

Agadir Agreement FTA (Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 120 of 2016; Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2002 issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003, as amended; Anti-Terrorism Law No. 94 of 2015; Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment and its Executive Regulations (PM Decree No. 2310 of 2017), imposing UBO disclosure obligations at GAFI; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) AML/CFT Compliance Regulations; Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) KYC/UBO rules; Egypt Financial Intelligence Unit (EG-FIU) reporting requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public of the shareholder's country of origin (certified true copy) or issuing state authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; documents must be legalized by the Egyptian embassy or consulate in the country of issuance)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / banker's confirmation of good standing for each UBO injecting capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or issuing bank of the UBO's primary account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization where bank is outside Egypt; notarized English/Arabic translation mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / registry excerpt for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (or apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is an apostille state AND the receiving Egyptian authority accepts it, which materially remains consular legalization in practice)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Power of Attorney appointing the local Egyptian registration attorney or GAFI service agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the foreign shareholder's country; countersigned by the Egyptian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and source-of-funds affidavit for each natural person holding or controlling 25% or more of equity or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder letters signed before a notary public (Egyptian or foreign, subsequently legalized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for foreign-issued signatures; Egyptian notary for domestic execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the EG-FIU consolidated lists, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated list, UK HMT list, CBE terrorist financing list, and Egyptian domestic court-issued freeze lists. Screening must be conducted prior to GAFI filing, repeated at incorporation, and whenever a shareholder or UBO change occurs. Low-risk digital publishing profile does not exempt the company from applying risk-based enhanced due diligence on any politically exposed person (PEP), family member, or close associate; source-of-funds verification is compulsory for bank account opening and for any cash contribution to share capital.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI E-Services Portal via the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (https://www.gafi.gov.eg) — Commercial Name Reservation and Company Incorporation e-module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company's name must be drafted in Arabic and is registered in Arabic as the controlling legal name; a Latin (English/French) transliteration may be recorded concurrently as a trade name provided it is a phonetically faithful transliteration of the Arabic name. The Arabic name governs all statutory instruments; the foreign-language version must appear on all outward commercial documents only as a secondary presentation. The name must clearly reflect the corporate form (LLC, 'ذا.م.م' or 'ذات مسؤولية محدودة' in Arabic) and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name, trademark, or protected commercial title in the GAFI database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Press (unless registered with the Supreme Council for Media Regulation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives an electronic notification identifying the conflicting token or similarity. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Committee within 15 working days of rejection, attaching a legal memorandum, trademark search certificate (if applicable), and the rejected reservation reference number. The Name Committee issues a decision within 15 working days after receipt of the appeal. If the rejection is grounded in a sensitive token, the applicant must first obtain a written no-objection letter from the relevant minister (e.g., Central Bank, Ministry of Information in the case of media-related words) and re-submit the name through the GAFI portal; the no-objection letter must be legalized and Arabized if issued by a foreign authority. A rejected name may be re-applied with a modified transliteration; filing a fresh application resets the 30-day reservation clock. Judicial appeal to the Cairo Economic Court is available after exhaustion of the administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office (postal mailbox without physical presence) is not permitted for LLC incorporation. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical Egyptian address, evidenced by a lease agreement or ownership title, a recent utility bill, and an inspection-accessible site. Shared serviced office space or a coworking desk meeting, with a physical lease and presence identifiable by the landlord and emergency authorities, is generally accepted for low-risk digital publishing; a 'virtual address' arrangement without any physical host is rejected at the registration stage or leads to administrative cancellation of the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for an ISIC 5813 digital magazine portal with low AML risk; the probability rises to 25–30% if the company engages in sponsored advertising payments or cross-border remittances without a local bank account, and to >40% if the registered address is a shared office shared with unrelated commercial entities. GAFI's Public Administration for Investment Complaints carries out field visits; the Commercial Registry may also verify the office during tax card issuance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law) as amended by Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment and Law No. 4 of 2022; Articles 102 to 117 for Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations promulgated by the Minister of Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Department and Commercial Registry (Cairo and governorate one-stop shops).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company (Company Contract) filed with the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for LLC under Law 159/1981; the capital stated in the Memorandum must be fully subscribed and the paid-up portion deposited in an Egyptian bank account in the company's name before incorporation, and the bank certificate must be attached to the GAFI filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers unanimously adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association and accept the paid-up share subscription allocated to each member. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at [lawful address within Egypt] and that the directors be authorized to execute the office lease and municipal registration. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] be appointed directors/managers, with [Name] as Managing Director and chief legal representative, and [Name] as Compliance Officer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that management may open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and procure the Commercial Registration, Tax Card, social insurance registration, and the operational clearance necessary for digital publishing. The managers are directed to file all statutory returns under Law 159/1981.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Pre-Incorporation Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OCO), Name Reservation Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application with three proposed Arabic/English names for the digital magazine portal. GAFI runs the names against the Trade Register and marks any identical or confusingly similar existing entity. A name clearance certificate is issued for 60 days.
required_dossiers: GAFI name clearance application form
Passport or national ID copies of all shareholders
Notarized power of attorney for the filing agent or applicant
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association for reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, the applicant may either file a written justified objection with the GAFI Trade Names Committee or immediately resubmit with alternate proposed names from the original clearance request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Notary Public / GAFI Legal Affairs Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Company Contract in Arabic, including corporate objects for digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements (ISIC 5813), share capital and division, manager appointment, and registered office. Arrange signature of all subscribers and notarization of the contract before competent notary; ensure Arabic limitation clause under Article 102.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Name clearance certificate
Registered office lease contract or property title
Passport/national ID copies and powers of attorney for all subscribers
Certificate of incorporation draft for managers' appointment clause
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary or GAFI legalization unit require corrections, execute an addendum to the Company Contract, re-issue all signatures, and renotarize within the validity period of the name clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Incorporation Bank Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Commercial Bank (National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, Commercial International Bank, or similar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation account in the future LLC's name using the notarized Company Contract. Deposit the paid-up portion of the subscribed capital and obtain a bank capital deposit certificate reflecting the exact share subscriptions. The certificate must be issued to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name clearance certificate
Shareholders' identification documents and signatures
Bank account opening application and KYC forms
Shareholders' subscription resolution authorizing the capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank files a suspicious transaction report or queries ultimate beneficial ownership, provide a written explanation, supporting source-of-funds documentation, and the signed BO registry declaration, then request expedited clearance from the AML compliance unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registration with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department and Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Company Contract, bank capital certificate, name clearance and standard GAFI establishment application to the one-stop shop. After statutory review, the LLC receives its commercial registration extract (Qayd al-Tijari), Tax Card and certificate of incorporation/formation number.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation form (Establishment Request Form)
Notarized Company Contract
Bank certificate of paid-up capital
Lease contract with owner's title or municipal extract
Copies of national IDs/passports of all managers
Declaration of the First Board Resolution appointing managers
GAFI foreign investment form if any shareholder is non-Egyptian
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried for missing documents, complete the shortfall through the OCO corrective-document window within 15 working days. For substantive rejection, file an administrative reconsideration with GAFI, and if still refused, appeal before the State Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Governance, Tax and Occupational Licensing Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI, District Local Administration, Tax Authority, Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to confirm the pro-forma resolutions, issue share certificates, appoint officers/secretary, open the permanent operating bank account, register for payroll and social insurance, obtain the municipal operating license, and secure civil defense clearance for the office. File the board resolution with the Commercial Registry where required.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution and signed minutes
Certificate of incorporation and commercial registration extract
Tax card and VAT registration forms
Social insurance registration form for employees
Municipal operating license application (Rukhsah Tashghil al-Mahal)
Fire safety and civil defense clearance
Environmental exemption/registration declaration for non-industrial office activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district office demands a physical inspection, coordinate an expedited site inspection within 30 days. If an environmental clearance is erroneously requested, furnish the EEAA exemption letter for office-only digital publishing activities. Civil defense deficiencies are corrected by installing required extinguishers and exit signage, followed by reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for non-industrial digital publishing; local municipal authority and GAFI one-stop shop govern the office establishment operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Extract (Qayd al-Tijari) and Municipal Operating License for Office Establishment (Rukhsah Tashghil al-Mahal)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C non-industrial office activity; no production process, effluent, or combustion emissions).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital magazine portal operations. The office must comply with Law 4/1994 on waste management by segregating municipal solid waste and contracting with licensed waste carriers; no wastewater or VOC thresholds are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Civil Defense fire-safety clearance for the office premises, including portable fire extinguishers, illuminated exit signs, smoke detection where required, and an electrical load certificate. Municipal occupancy/structural clearance verifies safe load and means of egress. Workplace health and safety duties under Labor Law 12/2003 and Ministerial Decree 211/2007 apply once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt. Official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt clearance platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; e-filing/e-services platform: https://dgrtax.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Egyptian LLC obtains a unified Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the ETA within 30 days of issuance of the Commercial Registration (CR) certificate. Procedure: (1) Execute a notarized LLC Articles of Association (AOA) with a certified capital structure; obtain CR and Chamber of Commerce card from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI, for foreign-owned LLCs); (2) Appoint an Egypt-licensed tax representative or statutory auditor for all ETA filings if management is offshore; file the corporate Power of Attorney and board resolution with the ETA; (3) Submit the electronic registration application via the ETA e-registration module with: CR certificate, AOA, ISIC 5813 activity classification statement, IDs and tax domicile declarations of shareholders/managers, and an Egyptian bank account certificate; (4) Upon approval, obtain the unified TIN (per Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 Article 36) and the separate VAT registration certificate (TIN-VA) under VAT Law No. 67/2016; (5) Enroll in the mandatory e-invoicing system on the ETA platform and obtain the digital XML-signature certificates/QR token before issuing invoices. A non-resident entity with no Egyptian establishment that supplies digital content (including the digital magazine portal) to Egyptian consumers may instead apply for simplified direct VAT registration on the ETA Foreign Digital Services portal; this registration does not create a permanent establishment nor triggers CIT filing obligations, and applies solely to the 14% VAT on remote B2C digital services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or pass-through treatment for LLCs; the EG LLC is mandatorily a resident juridical person taxed on worldwide income at a 22.5% CIT rate. Available elections and reliefs: (a) VAT group registration election under Article 17 of Law 67/2016 allowing related Egyptian entities to be treated as one VAT person (ETA pre-approval required); (b) Election to conduct business inside a Qualified Economic Zone (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone/SCZone) under Investment Law No. 72/2017, which permits customs and indirect-tax suspension regimes for zone-inbound machinery and inputs (the digital magazine portal however is outside zone benefits unless the adjudication officer confirms the zone-boundary exemption); (c) Export income investment incentive election: up to 50% reduction of taxable export profits under Investment Law 72/2017, phased out in observance of WTO subsidy disciplines; (d) Election to use the ETA pro-rata input VAT recovery ratio (export zero-rated arm vs. domestic 14% taxable arm); (e) Election to apply deferred CIT installments for startup/subscale companies under ETA guidelines. No hybrid mismatch or entity-classification elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 mandatory annual taxable turnover threshold (Article 14, VAT Law No. 67/2016); voluntary VAT registration is permitted once taxable turnover reaches EGP 50,000 in any 12-month look-back. Non-resident digital-content suppliers (including foreign magazine portals) are compulsorily registrable on the ETA non-resident digital services module without turnover threshold when making B2C supplies to Egyptian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers. Each B2B invoice and B2C e-receipt must be generated through ETA-approved invoicing software and transmitted in near real-time (intra-day, at latest within 24 hours) to the ETA e-invoicing API in XML or JSON with a compliant XML digital signature. The ETA performs real-time schema validation, deduplication, tax-code cross-check and encodes a Unique Identifier (UUID) plus a QR code / barcode that must be printed or embedded on the issued document. Phased enforcement became fully mandatory for all VAT registrants during fiscal year 2023 and is strictly audited. Non-submission or rejection of an invoice by the ETA is legally equal to non-issuance of the invoice, leading to fines from EGP 1,000 up to EGP 50,000 per rejected document plus suspension of the taxpayer's e-invoice account.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and exported services are zero-rated at 0% under Article 21(1) and (3) of VAT Law No. 67/2016. For the digital magazine portal (ISIC 5813), the following cumulative tests must be satisfied: (a) supply is made to a non-resident subscriber, advertiser or B2B customer whose usual place of residence or business is outside Egypt (verified by subscriber BIN/payment-account country, IP-address geolocation and contractual domicile); (b) for digital subscriptions, the digital content is made available and downloaded/streamed by the non-resident customer outside Egypt; no Egyptian server-intellectual-rights test is applied; (c) for sponsored media placements, the advertising campaign is published/broadcast outside Egypt to non-resident audiences, or paid by the Egyptian entity only if the advertisement relates to an export transaction; where the sponsor documents an EG domestic audience or EG contractual counterparty, the supply is taxable at 14%; (d) consideration is settled in freely convertible foreign currency and is repatriated through an Egyptian bank account; (e) VAT invoices are issued through the ETA e-invoicing platform with zero-rated tax code and are linked to the underlying export evidence. Input VAT attributable to the zero-rated export arm is creditable and refundable through e-filing, subject to a six-month statutory refund claim window and ETA document verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (C31) / NAFEZA Egyptian Single Window export receipt containing the shipment/transaction metadata and official customs approval
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) issued in the exporter's name as shipper and the non-resident counterparty as consignee, carrying carrier stamp and date
Inward Remittance Certificate (IBC) or bank transfer advice from the Egyptian bank evidencing hard-currency receipt matching the invoice number and amount
Signed commercial invoice and underlying subscription/placement contract with the non-resident customer or advertiser
ETA-validated zero-rated e-invoice with UUID, QR code and the zero-rating tax code assigned by the e-invoicing platform
Place-of-supply evidence bundle for digital magazine services (payment-card BIN country, subscriber registered address declaration, IP-address geolocation logs and platform usage logs)
Freely convertible FX settlement proof when the counterparty is located in a listed non-cooperative target jurisdiction (additional ETA documentation may be requested)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA conducts segmented audits of export-ledgers, cross-referencing NAFEZA customs declarations, inbound remittance slips and subscriber/IP geolocation logs. Civil clawback: any restored, unaudited or disproved zero-rated export supply is re-assessed at the 14% standard VAT rate (or at the 20% additional tax under special cases for digital B2C supplies if applicable) plus default interest at 2% per month (24% annualized) from the original refund date. Administrative fines under Law 67/2016 apply from EGP 1,000 to EGP 50,000 per missing, forged or late supporting document. Criminal exposure under Articles 41-43 (as amended) applies where the exporter deliberately uses forged shipping documents, round-tripped invoices or fabricated subscriber remittances to obtain a VAT refund: imprisonment from 3 to 5 years and fines up to double the evaded tax or the amount of the fraudulently obtained refund. Additionally, if export proceeds are not received within the CBE prescription period (default 180 days from shipment/invoice), the zero-rating is retrospectively rescinded, the VAT becomes due in full, and Central Bank regulations impose an administrative penalty of 1% per month on the unrepatriated amount until settlement or exporter proof of force majeure is accepted by the CBE.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under Law No. 194 of 2020 promulgating the Central Bank and Banking System Law, together with its Executive Regulations and Foreign Exchange Law No. 38 of 1994, as amended
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF, so current account transactions are generally freely convertible and supported by licensed banks. Capital account transactions remain subject to CBE licensing and registration requirements. Profit remittances by non-resident shareholders of an Egyptian LLC are permissible upon submission of audited financial statements, a tax compliance certificate confirming payment of all Egyptian profits tax and withholding taxes, and a duly completed CBE-approved bank transfer request; practical delays and secondary FX documentation may arise during periods of external sector stress, but no formal blanket prohibition exists for a correctly lodged profit remittance flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For both merchandise and service exporters, including digital publication and advertising revenue exports derived through platforms such as Stripe and AdSense, CBE instructions require full repatriation of proceeds through a bank authorized in Egypt within 90 days from the date the income is accrued. A mandatory conversion ratio of at least 50% of the repatriated foreign currency amount to Egyptian pounds is currently applied at the time of the transaction; the remaining balance may be retained in a foreign currency account of the LLC at an Egyptian licensed bank. The CBE retains authority to raise or lower the mandatory conversion ratio by circular, and export proceeds must first be credited to an Egyptian bank account before any disbursement to foreign suppliers is made.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and/ or Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and/ or Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Moderate. Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., virtual multi-currency account services domiciled in the UK/EU) are not licensed by the CBE and cannot receive export proceeds directly in satisfaction of Egyptian surrender and repatriation requirements as the sole clearing route. Such EMIs can be used only as an ancillary collection mechanism if: (1) the primary settlement of export proceeds is ultimately routed to and fully disclosed to an Egyptian licensed bank, and (2) no residual funds remain in the EMI beyond that required for ongoing operational settlement. Purely offshore EMI wallets holding retained EGP-linked balances or converting EGP without CBE authorization would breach CBE foreign currency control rules and may trigger AML scrutiny.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatorily required for at least one director and, where a non-resident beneficial owner is identified, the beneficial owner must attend an interview at the bank's branch or at a designated representative office. Remote account opening is generally not permitted for Egyptian LLCs with non-resident shareholders, save for the exceptional case of pre-approved government-promoted digital onboarding pilots. All authorized signatories and directors over whom the bank must complete client due diligence should be prepared to appear with original passports, original corporate resolutions, and original commercial registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and certified true copies of passport pages for all shareholders, directors, and authorized signatories; apostilled or legalized constitutional documents (articles of association and LLC contract); board resolution approving account opening and appointing signatories; Evidence of legitimate economic purpose in Egypt (lease agreement or service contract for the digital publication headquarters); a detailed equity contribution and source-of-funds declaration with supporting audited bank statements of the ultimate shareholder(s).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital advertising and platform revenue with high transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed advertising agreements with overseas networks, AdSense/Stripe settlement statements covering at least 6 consecutive months, an annual projected cash-flow breakdown, tax registration cards and tax clearance certificate/Hunafat, and a letter of explanation confirming the business operates a bona fide digital magazine without licensing requirements under relevant Egyptian press or media standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unstructured third-party payments alleged to be trade payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, purchase orders, screening of counterparties against CBE's AML/CFT lists and international sanctions lists, KYC packs for each material third-party supplier, proof of delivery of digital advertising placements through metric reports, and intercompany/ownership chain charts to evidence the absence of fragmented beneficial-ownership concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Allege insufficient economic substance for an off-shore digital publisher
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: In Egypt: service premises in Cairo or New Administrative City with utility bills, three local full-time equivalents, board meeting minutes held in Egypt, Egyptian tax bookkeeping records, social insurance registrations, and an explanation of the multinational payment flows deployed for FX repatriation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for an Egyptian LLC's equity injection require the foreign shareholder to remit via SWIFT with purpose code corresponding to CBE's 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital in Egyptian Companies' (typically code 13S1 or equivalent as detailed in the current CBE coding manual). The receiving Egyptian bank must first verify the LLC is duly registered in the CBE's database through the Commercial Registry. The injection is then credited to the LLC's capital escrow account and must be released to the LLC's operational account only upon presentation of the recommendation letter of the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), the issued share premium statement, and a signed copy of the shareholder resolution. Regulatory approval under Article 80 of Law 194/2020 may be required if the remittance amount exceeds the published consultation threshold. Full beneficial ownership information and sworn declaration as to the non-criminally derived nature of the funds must accompany the wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements from an Egyptian LLC to foreign vendors take the form of SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for unescrowed payments and commercial letters of credit (LC) for high-value or recurring acquisition of digital content and licensing arrangements. Each outbound payment must be supported by the USD/EGP purpose code '5I15 - Services - Advertising' or '5I12 - Royalties and Broadcasting' as appropriate, and is routed via a bank-approved RAIS system where the bank conducts post-shipment and post-performance verification. Recurrent licensing or content licensing payments should be documented by an LC-favored frame agreement to establish commercial reality. All outbound FX will be settled against a Q2 Daily Corporate Foreign Currency Allowance and requires submission by the payee of the relevant invoice, tax invoicing statement, proof of services, and, when applicable, tax withholding certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts through licensed Egyptian banks
FX swaps contracted by banks under the CBE hedge book
Non-deliverable forwards with foreign counterparties offshore for STTR-related hedging (subject to CBE prior approval and underlying commercial exposure documentation)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign debt (upon CBE registration)
Plain vanilla FX forwards for commercial settlement risk, provided the underlying transactional exposure is evidenced by LC, invoices, or contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return with Audited Financial Statements (Form No. 41)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine EGP 500–5,000; delayed payment surcharge 2% per month of tax due, capped at 100%; tax clearance certificates withheld for banking and government transactions until settlement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Certificate Renewal (Annual Fee and 5-Year Re-Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, via GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal fee due each January; full certificate re-registration every 5 years from incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% for the first month of delay plus 2% for each additional month, capped at 100% of the fee; suspension of legal capacity and risk of administrative strike-off after repeated statutory warnings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Electronic UBO Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual re-confirmation due in January; mandatory update within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 up to EGP 200,000; suspension of GAFI and Commercial Registry transactions for the entity and its managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Chamber of Commerce Annual Membership Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce (local chamber at registered address)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% per month on the annual subscription; blocking of certificates of origin, commercial attestations, and export-related documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Stamp Duty Return on Corporate Documents (Law No. 111/1980)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 28 February covering the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay penalty of 1.5% per month on unpaid duty, capped at 100%; denial of tax clearance certificates required for bank account operations and legal proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs, irrespective of revenue, assets, or ownership composition, must appoint at least one licensed external auditor under Companies Law No. 159/1981; audited financial statements must be filed with the ETA — no small-company audit exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS) as issued by Ministerial Decree No. 110/2015, substantially aligned with IFRS; statutory accounts are prepared in Egyptian Pounds on a going-concern basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO data is submitted to GAFI's electronic UBO registry at formation and reconfirmed annually in January; every share transfer must be notarized, recorded in the Register of Members, filed with the Commercial Registry, and the UBO register updated within 30 days; failure to reflect transfers invalidates any subsequent dividend or voting exercise.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assembly and Manager Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 600 per year (virtual registered office and administrative address services in Cairo, including local correspondence and authorities notification)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 – 3,500 per year for a small digital-publishing LLC with international payment flows and cross-border receipts

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general preferential rate for digital publishing. A qualifying free-zone or Investment Law 72/2017 licensed project may access a statutory tax holiday or free-zone export exemption; however, a non-licensed digital magazine LLC remains subject to the standard 22.5% corporate income tax rate on Egyptian-sourced subscription and sponsored media income. Any free-zone exemption applies only to offshore export-facing activities, not to domestic Egyptian digital revenues.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 41 (annual corporate income tax return for juridical persons) submitted through the Egyptian Tax Authority e-services portal (eTax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance corporate income tax installments are due for calendar-year taxpayers in May, August, November, and February.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end the statutory deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax card number, commercial registration number, paid-in capital, registered address, date of incorporation, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian LLC's identifiers. Non-resident shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners are reported separately in the ownership annex; they are not co-taxpayers on the entity return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the tax year and accounting standard applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch must use the Egyptian Tax Authority-approved 12-month accounting period; any mismatch with the home-country fiscal year must be explained in the return notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Business Activity and License Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC / NAICS classification for digital magazine publishing and sponsored media portals, including any SCZONE or Investment Authority license number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned LLC, state the Egyptian permanent establishment or branch registration if applicable. Absence of a statutory license does not waive the filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All digital subscriptions, AdSense revenues, sponsored placements, native advertising, and content monetization proceeds before deduction of expenses, translated into EGP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile declared revenue with Stripe and AdSense settlement reports. Egyptian-source service income and foreign-source income must be segregated; DTA-derived no-permanent-establishment positions must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Cost of Sales and Direct Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Editorial staff costs, content license fees, hosting and bandwidth, digital production, and amortization of internally developed content.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border related-party content license fees must be at arm's length and supported by Egyptian transfer pricing local file documentation when the threshold is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing costs, payment processor fees, platform fees, legal and accounting expenses, and general administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Parent-office cost recharges must reflect actual services received, be evidenced by service agreements, and are subject to Egyptian withholding tax on cross-border service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net interest paid or accrued on shareholder loans and external debt, after applying thin capitalization and arm's-length financing rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident lender is subject to statutory 10% withholding tax; deductibility requires supporting loan agreements, transfer pricing analysis, and proof that the borrowing funds Egyptian operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax itself, late-payment surcharges, administrative fines, unsupported accruals, non-business entertainment, excessive bad-debt provisions, and disallowed depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch addbacks must be identified separately so the home jurisdiction can properly compute foreign tax credit eligibility and avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of carried-forward tax losses available from prior years, limited to five consecutive taxable years and subject to continuity-of-ownership conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch may offset only losses derived from the Egyptian permanent establishment, provided prior-year returns were filed on time. Losses of a foreign head office cannot be set off against Egyptian profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net taxable profit after legal deductions, addbacks, and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities, include only income effectively connected with an Egyptian permanent establishment; otherwise claim treaty no-permanent-establishment status with supporting activity evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax before credits calculated as Taxable Income multiplied by 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same 22.5% rate applies to a non-resident branch; no reduced non-resident statutory rate is available in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance installment payments, foreign tax credits, and withholding tax credits on interest and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter treaty foreign tax credits only with official foreign tax receipts. Excess Egyptian withholding may be refundable through the Egyptian Tax Authority's treaty relief procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 13 - Net Tax Payable or Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance payable with the return or any overpayment to be refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must settle the balance from an Egyptian bank account; refunds are payable only after tax audit and through Egyptian banking channels.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Controlled transaction schedule listing related parties, jurisdictions, transaction types, values, and selected OECD transfer pricing methods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for all cross-border controlled transactions with no minimum value; include the TP disclosure form in the annual return and attach Local or Master File when statutory thresholds are exceeded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020, non-filing or late filing triggers an administrative fine of at least EGP 10,000 and up to EGP 200,000. Unpaid tax accrues a late-payment surcharge of 1.5% per month or part of a month from the due date until full settlement. A materially false or evasive return exposes the entity and responsible directors to criminal prosecution under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005.
